title: Application CRD gains `initiatedBy` — apply the 2.11 CRDs with the upgrade

detection.reason: the CRD's schema is not collected, so whether the installed Application CRD already carries initiatedBy cannot be settled from the inventory

quote: In order to address argoproj/argo-cd#16612, initiatedBy has been added in the Application CRD.
remediation: Upgrade the CRDs together with the controllers (the install manifests include them); a Helm install must have `crds.install` enabled or apply the CRDs separately, or the new field is rejected on write.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd applications.argoproj.io -o json | jq '[.. | objects | select(has("initiatedBy"))] | length' # 0 = the installed CRD predates 2.11; apply the 2.11 CRDs

title: `argocd-redis` NetworkPolicy loses its Egress restrictions from 2.11.2

detection.reason: fires when the stock redis/haproxy NetworkPolicy exists — its Egress section is what the 2.11.2 manifests open up

quote: Starting with Argo CD 2.11.2, the NetworkPolicy for the `argocd-redis` and `argocd-redis-ha-haproxy` dropped Egress restrictions. This change was made to allow access to the Kubernetes API to create a secret to secure Redis access.
remediation: If your policy required Redis to be egress-locked, add back an Egress rule that allows the Kubernetes API plus the traffic Redis itself needs (the note's example), instead of the unrestricted egress the new manifests ship.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get networkpolicy -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("redis")) | .metadata.name + ": egress=" + (.spec.egress | tostring | .[0:120])' # a redis policy printed with egress=null or [] restricts nothing after the upgrade
